title: Minimum Number of Operations to Transform a Sequence
description: Given two integer arrays `target` and `arr` of equal length without duplicates in `target`, find minimum operations to make `arr` a subsequence of `target` (insertions to arr). Equivalently: `length - LCS(target, arr)`.
input_format: First line contains `n`. Second line contains `target`. Third line contains `arr`.
hints: Map each element in `arr` to its index in `target`.
Filter elements of `arr` that do not appear in `target`.
Finding LCS reduces to finding the Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS) on mapped indices in O(N log N).

reference_solution:
import sys, bisect
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
if data:
    n = int(data[0])
    target = [int(x) for x in data[1:1+n]]
    arr = [int(x) for x in data[1+n:]]
    pos = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(target)}
    mapped = [pos[x] for x in arr if x in pos]
    tails = []
    for x in mapped:
        idx = bisect.bisect_left(tails, x)
        if idx == len(tails): tails.append(x)
        else: tails[idx] = x
    print(len(target) - len(tails))
